    Distribution of the L1 norm of the Brownian bridge

    p_l1_bridge.Rd

    The limiting null distribution of \(\sqrt{n}\,U^*_{pit}\). For a standard Brownian bridge \(B\), Johnson & Killeen (1983) give the c.d.f. of \(L = \int_0^1 |B(t)|\,\mathrm{d}t\) as the convergent series

    p_l1_bridge(q, terms = 30L)

q_l1_bridge(p, terms = 30L)

    Arguments

    q

    a vector of quantiles (non-negative)

    terms

    number of terms of the series to sum (default `30` [integer])

    p

    a vector of probabilities

    Value

    p_l1_bridge() returns the c.d.f. evaluated at q; q_l1_bridge() returns the quantile function evaluated at p

    Details

    $$P(L \le \ell) = \sqrt{\pi/2} \sum_{j=1}^{\infty} \delta_j^{-3/2} \psi(\ell / \delta_j^{3/2})$$

    with \(\psi(t) = 3^{2/3} t^{-1/3} e^{-2/(27 t^2)} Ai((3t)^{-4/3})\) and \(\delta_j = |a'_j| / 2^{1/3}\), where \(a'_j\) is the \(j\)th zero of \(Ai'\). Terms are suppressed by \(e^{-2/(27t^2)}\) with \(t = q/\delta_j^{3/2}\), so the number of terms needed grows with q. The default is ample over the whole range where the upper tail is numerically distinguishable from zero; beyond q = 10 the c.d.f. is returned as exactly 1.

    Unit tests

    

# the mean of the L1 norm of the bridge is known exactly to be sqrt(2 pi)/8
m = integrate(function(x) 1 - p_l1_bridge(x), 0, 5, subdivisions = 500L)$value
testthat::expect_equal(m, sqrt(2 * pi) / 8, tolerance = 1e-5)

# a proper distribution function
testthat::expect_equal(p_l1_bridge(0), 0)
testthat::expect_equal(p_l1_bridge(10), 1)
testthat::expect_true(all(diff(p_l1_bridge(seq(0.05, 1, 0.05))) > 0))

# and its inverse
testthat::expect_equal(p_l1_bridge(q_l1_bridge(0.95)), 0.95, tolerance = 1e-6)
